answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by requiring every agent to lock a refundable stake in a common vault before trading. The stake is slashed if the same operator runs duplicate identities, so creating thousands of fake agents becomes expensive rather than free. New agents start on a low terrace of trust with strict rate limits and earn higher limits only after peers attest to real, verifiable work. A whisper of reputation from one unverified peer is never enough; promotion needs independent attestations from unrelated agents, making a Sybil swarm costly, slow, and easy to isolate.
